text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Tens of thousands of Belgraders protest over annullment of election results for the fourteenth day, while opposition leaders call on them to exercise restriant and not submit to provocations.

- Several Serbian Supreme court judges sent an open letter to Nasa Borba and Politika demanding the truth about election results. Judge Zoran Ivosevic says he does not accept the judiciary's "subservient role which turns elections into self-appointment"

- Over 2,500 workers of the Motor and Tractors industry IMT announced they were to go on strike demanding payment of outstanding wages and to join protests against the theft votes at recent local elections.

- Yugoslav economists seminar says the government's 1997 economic policy is unrealistic because it does not deal with a number of unresolved issues such as the foreign debt, type of financial relations with the world and conditions of trade.
- The Serbian Police Force has stepped up mobilisation of its reserve police, adding them to units brought to Belgrade from Kosovo and southern Serbia, the paper learns.
- The constituent session of the Chamber of Citizens of the Yugoslav parliament will be held on December 10.
POLITIKA

- Serbian government says unexpected problems were posed in the realisation of economic and social functions caused mainly by parties who express dissatisfaction with election results by street demonstrations.

- The Anglo-Yugoslav bank, with a majority Yugoslav stake, preparing to establish credit lines with leading European and British banks to finance Yugoslav economy, says chairman of the board of directors Borka Vucic.
- Yugoslav firms open exhibition in Greece today, expected to open new possibilities of economic cooperation between the two countries.
- Czhech economic exhibiton opens at Belgrade fair today through December 6.
- The largest copper mine in Majdanpek will be closed early in 1997 after 35 years of expliatation. $80 million is needed to remove barren soil and reach new deposits.
- Serbian Education Minister says universities should secure unobstructed education and are not places for party competition.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Taxi drivers decide not to raise rates but agree to stop giving 20 and 30 percent reductions for calls.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Yugoslav and Montenegrin merchant fleets resume sailing after lifting of sanctions but their gains are eaten up by outstanding debts.
BORBA
- Prseident of Belgrade's first municipal court Dragoljub Jankovic says the court has not declared the election winner but only ruled for elections to be repeated in places where there were doubts.
